_meta.note: Merchant-curated pairings. THE single source for what goes with what. Seeded into `product_bundles` by ProductBundleSeeder; read directly by backend/api.js in the static build.
_meta.why: A storefront with no order history has no co-purchase data, and calling a guess 'frequently bought together' is a claim about other customers that has not happened. These are pairings the merchant stands behind, labelled as such. BundleService prefers real co-purchase counts the moment enough orders exist, and only then does the wording change to 'frequently bought together'.
_meta.rule: Every bundle states WHY its members belong together, in `reason`, in words a customer would recognise. If a reason cannot be written, the bundle is not real and should not ship.

bundles.title: The pour-over setup
bundles.reason: Coarse-ground beans, the cone and carafe to brew them in, and glasses that show the colour. Everything the method needs, nothing it doesn't.

bundles.title: The dates-and-honey table
bundles.reason: Medjool dates, Sidr honey and pistachios are the three things that end up on the same plate at iftar and at every gathering after it.

bundles.title: Build a cheese board
bundles.reason: Aged Gouda wants something sweet and something with bite next to it. Walnuts and dried apricots are what a cheesemonger would hand you.

bundles.title: The tea tray
bundles.reason: One black, one green, and the double-wall glasses that keep both hot without burning your hand.

bundles.title: The baking shelf
bundles.reason: Full-cream powder and grass-fed butter are the two dairy staples almost every recipe starts from, and cashews go into most of what comes out.

bundles.title: Morning routine, in order
bundles.reason: Vitamin-C serum, then moisturiser, then sunscreen. That order matters — vitamin C needs to reach skin first, and SPF has to go on last or it does nothing.

bundles.title: The three pans you actually use
bundles.reason: Cast iron for the slow things, nonstick for the fast ones, and one knife sharp enough that neither is a chore.

bundles.title: The desk, sorted
bundles.reason: Dotted paper, pens that don't skip, and somewhere to put them that isn't the drawer.

bundles.title: Drafting kit
bundles.reason: Three lead widths and dotted paper — the combination people who sketch technical work reach for.

bundles.title: Leather that ages together
bundles.reason: Full-grain weekender and full-grain belt take on the same patina, and the scarf covers the one gap a weekend bag leaves.

bundles.title: The layer for a Dhaka December
bundles.reason: Merino handles a cold morning without the bulk, and the scarf handles the hour before the sun gets up.

bundles.title: Start a connected home
bundles.reason: The Matter hub is the piece that makes everything else talk to each other; the speaker is usually the first thing people connect to it.

bundles.title: Over-ear at the desk, in-ear on the move
bundles.reason: Noise-cancelling cans for long sessions, buds for the commute, and a watch that controls both without reaching for a phone.

bundles.title: Prototype a sensor board
bundles.reason: Blank FR-4, the I²C temp/humidity sensor, the relay it switches, and the tactile switch and bulk capacitor every board of this kind ends up needing.

bundles.title: A gift that needs no wrapping
bundles.reason: Swiss dark chocolate and Medjool dates arrive presentation-ready; the grooming set turns two food gifts into one that works for anybody.

bundles.title: Fill the nut jar
bundles.reason: Raw almonds to snack on, cashews to cook with, walnuts for everything else. Buying the three together is how most kitchens stay stocked.

bundles.title: Polymer and board stock
bundles.reason: ABS pellets for enclosures and FR-4 blanks for what goes inside them — the two raw stocks a small production run draws down fastest.

bundles.title: For the glare
bundles.reason: Polarised lenses cut the glare your eyes notice; SPF 50 handles the part they don't.

bundles.title: Coffee, the everyday way
bundles.reason: Skimmed powder keeps without a fridge, which is the reason it and a bag of beans end up on the same shelf in most offices.
